title.narrative: Promoting Spaces for Conflict Prevention and Reduced Vulnerability in Abyei: A Joint Programme of the RCs in Sudan and South Sudan in Abyei (hereafter the UN Joint Programme in Abyei

description.narrative: Briefly describe the overall development challenge and the expected results of the project.One year after the outbreak of the conflict in Sudan, more than 17,000 South Sudanese returnees have crossed into Abyei Administrative Area (Abyei AA), some with intentions of heading to South Sudan or to return to their respective communities once the security situation allows. While most of the population has moved on to South Sudan, a significant number of these people have remained in Abyei, where they have family ties including because of proximity. In addition, as of May 2024, close to 18,000 members of the Misseriya tribe, driven by conflict have crossed into Abyei, where they have remained and settled in the Northern part of Abyei. At the same time, close to 4,000 displaced persons, including refugees, mostly of Eritrean and Somali origin have crossed into Abyei from different parts of Sudan and settled into communities with no support. Due to the disputed nature of the Abyei AA there is a heightened sense of marginalization and exclusion dramatically exacerbated by the ongoing conflict in Sudan and instability in South Sudan. Access to the northern part of the box from Sudan has become more challenging, with the disruption of air corridors due to the war and the subsequent limited humanitarian assistance. While development and peacebuilding activities remain challenging in the north, due to the unresolved political complexities, in the southern part of the box, there are more implementing partners, however the remoteness, and sole dependency on supply chains from South Sudan (Sudan supply chains being disrupted) continue to present challenges including but not limited to the higher prices of commodities and transport fees. The Abyei AA is currently classified as IPC 4 , where the entire population needs some form of humanitarian assistance. Reaffirming its commitment to support the unprecedented efforts by the RCs/HCs in Sudan and South Sudan in joint implementation
